newsitem.title: USA: Carpenter sees fiscal Q2 in line with yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Carpenter sees fiscal Q2 in line with yr ago.

text.p: Carpenter Technology Corp should post fiscal second quarter earnings that are "pretty much in line" with earnings from the year-earlier quarter, Robert Cardy, Carpenter's chairman, president and chief executive officer, said Tuesday.

At a luncheon meeting with reporters, Cardy said earnings for the second quarter of fiscal 1997, ended December 31, should be "pretty much in line" with the $0.69 per share the company posted in the second quarter of fiscal 1996.
Wall Street's consensus estimate for the 1997 quarter is $0.77 per share.

Moreover, Carpenter's earnings should be "back on track" in fiscal 1998, Cardy said. The company said earlier Tuesday that its fiscal 1997 earnings for the year ending June 30 would be lower than fiscal 1996 earnings of $3.51 per share.
The company cited customer inventory adjustments in some industries and the need for Carpenter to reduce its own inventories as reasons for the lower earnings.
Carpenter shares were down 1-7/8 in late afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
"I don't expect to carry this baggage into '98," Cardy said. "I think in fiscal '98 we're going to be right back on track with our earnings."
Commenting on his outlook for 1998, Cardy said, "I don't see any danger signs ahead.... The company is in good shape."
Cardy also said his company's acquisition of Dynamet Inc would be accretive to earnings.
The company said earlier Tuesday it would acquire Dynamet, a privately held manufacturer of titanium bar, wire and powder products, for about $150 million in stock and cash.

Cardy said the acquisition should close in March. Carpenter, based in Reading, Pa., is the nation's largest producer of specialty steel long products and also makes engineered products including ceramics.
